text:
Andrei Svechnikov has found his shot: 13 goals in 24 games, 7 in his last ten, including two in the Hurricanes' 7-4 comeback over Edmonton on Nov. 21. The 26-year-old won a Stanley Cup with Carolina last spring, and the Hurricanes take 61% of the expected goals at five on five with him on. That's dominance.

His shooting, 19.1%, is above the 12.9% to 17.3% range our numbers see as his true talent, and he has 13 goals on 10.6 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances). But the chances themselves are up, 1.52 expected goals per 60 from 1.27 last season. Evolving-Hockey had a cost flagged last season: opponents created more with him on than with all but 6% of forwards. It's worth watching whether that has changed with this team's dominance. Then there's the flair. North State Journal's Cory Lavalette reported Svechnikov saying of a lacrosse-goal try, "I didn't have the room there, but it's going to come, maybe one of them this season." Our numbers project 30 to 44 goals.
headline: Svechnikov's shot is landing for the champions
